data.why: The dashboard's own 'Configuration' selector reads directly from experiments/configs/*.yaml already in the repo (bff_dev.yaml is a fast ~512-organism, 200-epoch smoke config); the simulation starts from randomly generated programs, so there is no external dataset or upload for a scientist to supply.

goals: Start a fresh BFF primordial-soup run from the bff_dev config and watch the population grid and diversity/entropy/complexity metrics evolve epoch by epoch
Inspect an individual organism's genome, generation, parents, and instruction distribution using the genome inspector
Step through the BFF execution of a paired tape by hand in the execution debugger to see exactly how two genomes interact
Run a replication scan over a population sample to flag candidate self-replicators and classify them
Resume a previously checkpointed run from the run browser and continue stepping it forward
Compare metric histories (e.g. unique_genomes, dominant_genome_frequency) across multiple stored runs

review.summary: The tree states what the tool is for, following the README's live-run, organism-inspection, execution-debugging, replicator-scan, resume and compare workflow. Phases and features are well cut, and every screen I opened matches its node. It needs small fixes before filing: fold the duplicate seed task into t1, record the lineage KeyError and overlay problems the replay found, and note the configs and scan-to-inspector path that were never exercised.
